--- title: "R for data analysis" subtitle: "Beginner course · Master GPE (CERDI / IHEDD)" description: "Six sessions to learn R: import, manipulate, describe, visualise and report development data." --- Six sessions to learn R from scratch, for **Master GPE** students (development economics). **No prerequisites**: you start by installing R and finish with a reproducible report built on World Bank data. ::: {.hero-actions} [Start Session 1](seances/seance-1.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg} [Download the data](data.zip){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-lg} ::: ## The six sessions ```{=html}
Session 1

Getting started with R and RStudio

Interface, objects, functions, packages, RStudio projects and paths with here().

 Session 2

Importing and exporting data

CSV, Excel, malformed files; cleaning column names; saving your results.

 Session 3

Data manipulation

dplyr, tidyr, joins: filter, transform, aggregate, merge sources.

 Session 4

Descriptive statistics and regression

Summarising data, correlations, linear regression and its limits.

 Session 5

Visualising with ggplot2 (and maps)

Grammar of graphics, scatter plots, time series, world maps.

 Session 6

Advanced visualisation and Quarto reports

Interactive charts, the final figure and a reproducible Quarto report.
``` ::: {.secondary-links} **Also:** [Dataviz workshop](slides/atelier-dataviz.qmd) (slides, in French) · [Resources](resources.qmd): books, documentation, data sources ::: ## Where we are going > **Common thread: growth, health and inequality, what does the data say about developing countries?** ```{=html}
  1. R and RStudio
  2. Import
  3. Manipulate
  4. Describe
  5. Visualise
  6. Report
``` **Import** data, **manipulate** it, **describe** it, **visualise** it, then **report** it: each session adds one link to the chain. By Session 5 you will produce charts like this one: **richer countries live longer, but the gain flattens out** (the "Preston curve"). Every point is a country; the area shows its population. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Show the code (you will write this in Session 5)"} wdi <- read_csv(here("data", "wdi_panel.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) # CAF life expectancy is unreliable in this WDI release (14.7 in 2009, 18.8 in 2022): exclude every year wdi <- wdi |> mutate(life_exp = if_else(iso3c == "CAF", NA_real_, life_exp)) wdi |> filter(year == 2019, !is.na(gdp_pc_ppp), !is.na(life_exp), !is.na(region)) |> ggplot(aes(x = gdp_pc_ppp, y = life_exp, size = population, colour = region)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + scale_x_log10(labels = label_dollar(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) + scale_size_area(max_size = 12, guide = "none") + scale_colour_manual(values = pal_regions, labels = label_wrap(25)) + guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 3, override.aes = list(size = 3))) + labs( title = "Richer countries live longer, with diminishing returns", x = "GDP per capita (constant 2021 PPP $, log scale)", y = "Life expectancy at birth (years)", colour = NULL, caption = "Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators (WDI), 2019. Bubble area = population." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/hero-preston-1.png){fig-alt='Bubble chart of life expectancy against GDP per capita (log scale) for countries in 2019, coloured by region, bubble area proportional to population. Life expectancy rises with income, with diminishing gains at higher incomes.' width=768} ::: ::: ## Before the first session ::: {.callout-important} ## To do at home 1. Install **R**: . 2. Install **RStudio Desktop**: (after R). 3. In RStudio: *File > New Project > New Directory* and create a project folder named `r-course`. 4. Download **[data.zip](data.zip)** and unzip it **into the `r-course` folder**, so that `data/` and `R/theme_cours.R` sit next to the `.Rproj` file (`here::here()` relies on this). 5. Install the packages: paste the block below in the RStudio **Console** and run it **once**. It takes a few minutes. ::: ```r install.packages(c("tidyverse", "here", "janitor", "readxl", "writexl", "lubridate", "scales", "WDI", "gt", "fixest", "modelsummary", "ggrepel", "sf", "rnaturalearth", "rnaturalearthdata", "patchwork", "plotly", "crosstalk", "shiny")) ``` Expected folder tree: ``` r-course/ ├── r-course.Rproj ├── data/ │ ├── wdi_panel.csv │ ├── ... │ └── raw/ └── R/ └── theme_cours.R ``` ## How to use this site - Every session follows the same plan: objectives, explanations with code, **exercises**, then "Key takeaways". - Type the code yourself in RStudio rather than copying it: that is how you learn. - **Solutions are collapsed**: try first, then open to compare. - An error is not a failure: read the message, it almost always says what is wrong. ## AI and code AI assistants can explain an error message or an unfamiliar function. They must not replace your learning. **Always run the suggested code and understand every line** before using it: code that runs is not necessarily correct. --- Content licensed [CC BY-NC-ND 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/), like pierrebeaucoral.github.io.
